When the existing adapter returns Paused or Running, the old behavior returned that outcome immediately so a paused grant could be resolved later and a timeout remained a timeout. This code instead calls daemon.Review again every second until the 30-minute deadline; for a paused run, Review resumes the same grant automatically. missed.defect: Starting the parallel Greenhouse process is performed synchronously before the built-in Review Round is started, and any error from startParallelGreenhouseReviews is returned immediately. Thus a Greenhouse startup failure, ledger/notice failure, lock error, or owner-file error prevents the built-in review from starting, contrary to the contract that Greenhouse failure or refusal must never delay the built-in loop.

A transient adapter error is recorded as a failed request row before retrying, then a later successful retry records a second verdict row. The comparison consequently counts one logical request multiple times and lowers reliability for recoverable failures, even though the request ultimately settled without manual action.

unmatched.explanation: The new polling loop applies to non-parallel Greenhouse reviews as well as shadow reviews. When the existing adapter returns Paused or Running, the old behavior returned that outcome immediately so a paused grant could be resolved later and a timeout remained a timeout. This code instead calls daemon.Review again every second until the 30-minute deadline; for a paused run, Review resumes the same grant automatically. That changes existing review behavior even when review_parallel is unset, contrary to the feature contract, and can make a normal command block for the full timeout or resume work that previously required a later invocation.
unmatched.action: Restrict the retry/poll loop to parallelMode, preserving the prior single daemon.Review call and immediate Running/Paused handling for non-parallel reviews.

adjudications.rationale: The finding concerns repeated polling and changed non-parallel review behavior, not duplicate request rows from retrying a transient adapter error, as shown by "Restrict the retry/poll loop to parallelMode".

model_findings.explanation: Provider selection is evaluated for the whole Task, not the requested workspace Member. If a workspace plan has one Greenhouse Member and another builtin full-pipeline Member, taskUsesGreenhouseGate returns true because the plan-level provider is Greenhouse, so isFullPipelineTask returns false even for the builtin Member. Existing candidate, validation, CI-fix, merge, and review-fix paths that call isFullPipelineTask(member) therefore skip the builtin Member's required private-candidate pipeline and can treat it as a non-full-pipeline lane.
model_findings.action: Make the full-pipeline classification provider-aware for the supplied repository, using the frozen Member provider (and the configured fallback only where appropriate), so a Greenhouse Member is excluded without disabling builtin full-pipeline Members in the same workspace.

missed.defect: For a workspace task, taskUsesGreenhouseReviewProvider(..., "") returns true when any admitted Member uses Greenhouse. Callers treat this task-wide result as if every Member were Greenhouse: startReviewRound refuses all built-in Review Tasks and signal skips the normal review-cap/carry reconciliation. A workspace with one Greenhouse Member and one builtin Member, which the admitted plan format explicitly supports, therefore cannot run the builtin review flow for the builtin Member.

GreenhouseGatePass selects the newest Greenhouse verdict for a repository without filtering to mode='gate'. A later parallel/shadow verdict therefore makes an earlier passing gate verdict fail Qualifies because its mode is parallel, even when both verdicts are for the same exact head. The merge and publication barriers can consequently reject a valid passing gate after a shadow review is recorded.

model_findings.explanation: The selected review provider is only persisted in the admitted plan; runtime review and merge-gate paths do not read it. They still select built-in Review Tasks and evidence from plan.Review, while Greenhouse requests are driven only by the separate review_parallel setting. Consequently, admitting a Task with review_provider = "greenhouse" neither skips the built-in Review Task/private-candidate flow nor requests and requires a passing Greenhouse Verdict; a Task with no built-in review requirement can pass without any Greenhouse Verdict.
model_findings.action: Use the frozen provider from the admitted plan when dispatching review work and evaluating merge evidence. For greenhouse, invoke the Greenhouse adapter per changed Member, skip the built-in Review Task/private-candidate/validate path, and require an exact-head passing Verdict for every applicable Member; preserve the existing builtin path.
